edition.window: Orders and decisions passed or reported between 10:00 AM IST on 6 October 2026 and 10:45 AM IST on 7 October 2026

items.caseName: J.C. Flowers Asset Reconstruction Pvt. Ltd. v. Stargaze Entertainment Pvt. Ltd.
items.coram: Ashok Kumar Bhardwaj (Judicial Member), Atul Chaturvedi (Technical Member)
items.headline: Stargaze resolution plan rejected; liquidation ordered
items.text: The Tribunal refused to approve Cine Corp Filmdom's resolution plan for Stargaze Entertainment and directed liquidation. It found the CIRP vitiated because the resolution professional never secured control of the company's assets, and said commercial wisdom cannot justify a token recovery while substantial assets remain untraced.

items.caseName: IDBI Bank Limited v. Smt. Raj Kumari Garg
items.coram: Justice Anupinder Singh Grewal (President), Ravindra Chaturvedi (Technical Member)
items.headline: Guarantor not discharged by loan restructuring she did not sign
items.text: A personal guarantor stays liable even though she did not sign the later restructuring documents, because the original guarantee expressly allowed such variations. The Tribunal rejected the plea that the changes or release of mortgaged property discharged her and admitted IDBI Bank's Section 95 petition.

items.caseName: Nivedita Tiwari v. Nex Fitzap Private Limited & Ors.
items.coram: Bidisha Banerjee (Judicial Member), Rekha Kantilal Shah (Technical Member)
items.headline: Denying records and forcing cheap share sale is oppression
items.text: Shutting a director-shareholder out of financial records, pressing her to sell shares at an undervalued price and withholding her remuneration was held to be oppression. The bench also held she was entitled to at least a 25% royalty on a patented medical invention she developed and directed release of her suspended pay.

items.caseName: Hemanshu Jetley v. Punjab National Bank & Ors.
items.coram: Khetrabasi Biswal (Judicial Member), Shishir Agarwal (Technical Member)
items.headline: Interim finance to clear estate dues is CoC's call
items.text: The Tribunal allowed about ₹10.23 crore to be raised as interim finance from the successful resolution applicant to clear disputed estate office dues. Paying under protest while contesting the disputed part was held to be a commercial decision within the Committee of Creditors' domain.

items.caseName: Union of India v. Mary Matha Popular Nidhi Limited
items.coram: Vinay Goel (Judicial Member), Ravichandran Ramasamy (Technical Member)
items.headline: Popular Finance: 14 group entities ordered wound up
items.text: Acting on the SFIO's investigation into the Popular Finance group, the Tribunal ordered the winding up of 14 group companies. The Official Liquidator was appointed as Company Liquidator to take charge of the process.

items.caseName: Diipesh Lakshman Bhagtani v. The Registrar of Companies, Mumbai
items.coram: Hariharan Neelakanta Iyer (Technical Member), Lakshmi Gurung (Judicial Member)
items.headline: Struck-off company restored for its valuable contracts
items.text: The Tribunal restored MDED Estates Private Limited to the register, holding that a subsisting development agreement and valuable property are just grounds for restoration despite years of unfiled returns. Restoration was made subject to ₹3 lakh in costs. The order is dated 11 September 2026.

items.caseName: Movemate Logistics Private Limited v. OYO Hotels Private Limited
items.coram: Chitra Hankare (Judicial Member), Dr. V.G. Venkata Chalapathy (Technical Member)
items.headline: Movemate's insolvency plea against OYO rejected
items.text: The Tribunal dismissed a ₹2.10 crore operational-debt petition over warehousing and transport charges, finding the claims disputed and unverified. The parties' dispute is already in arbitration proceedings before the Delhi High Court. The order is dated 29 September 2026.

items.caseName: Sandeep Tiwari v. Gainwell Commosales Private Limited
items.coram: Dr. Sanjay Kumar Chandhariyavi (Judicial Member), Sungita Sharma (Technical Member)
items.headline: Commissioner's nod can't save appeal below ₹20 lakh
items.text: A departmental appeal involving about ₹11.88 lakh was dismissed as below the ₹20 lakh monetary limit. A bare statement that the Commissioner approved the appeal does not override the limit unless a recognised exception applies. The order is dated 1 October 2026.

items.caseName: Dalmia Cement (Bharat) Ltd. v. Commissioner, CGST & CX, Ranchi
items.coram: R. Muralidhar (Judicial Member), K. Anpazhakan (Technical Member)
items.headline: Civil works billed per cubic metre aren't manpower supply
items.text: Civil construction work priced per unit of work done is not 'manpower supply' just because the contractor used its own workers. The reverse-charge service tax demand on Dalmia Cement was set aside.

items.caseName: MP Online Ltd. v. Principal Commissioner of Customs, Central Excise and Service Tax, Bhopal
items.caseNo: Service Tax Appeal Nos. 50418 of 2017, 51646 of 2018 & 52763 of 2019
items.coram: Dr. Rachna Gupta (Officiating President), P.V. Subba Rao (Technical Member)
items.headline: Government data portal is not an OIDAR service
items.text: Service tax demands of about ₹41.56 crore against MP Online were set aside: running a portal through which citizens access government data is not an OIDAR service. Interest on fixed deposits and services to government bodies and educational institutions were also held not taxable as business support services.

items.caseName: M/s Northern Coalfields Limited v. Commissioner of Central GST, Central Excise & Customs
items.coram: Dr. Rachna Gupta (Officiating President), P.V. Subba Rao (Technical Member)
items.headline: RCM credit on pre-GST levies to be refunded in cash
items.text: Payments to Madhya Pradesh for the rural infrastructure tax and forest transit fee (April 2016 to June 2017) were held to be fees for services liable to service tax under reverse charge. Any CENVAT credit arising from that tax must be refunded in cash under Section 142 of the CGST Act.

items.caseName: Amsons Tours & Travels Pvt. Ltd. v. Commissioner of CGST & Central Excise, Mumbai East
items.coram: Ajay Sharma (Judicial Member), M.M. Parthiban (Technical Member)
items.headline: Appeal can't fail for want of pre-deposit proof already on record
items.text: An appeal cannot be thrown out for missing proof of pre-deposit when the appellate authority's own order records the payment; the appellant should get a chance to cure such lapses. The matter was sent back for a decision on merits. The order is dated 1 October 2026.

items.caseName: LTS Investment Fund Ltd v. Securities and Exchange Board of India
items.coram: Justice P.S. Dinesh Kumar (Presiding Officer), Meera Swarup, Dr. Dheeraj Bhatnagar (Technical Members)
items.headline: Hindenburg-named Mauritius funds' appeals disposed of
items.text: Five Mauritius-based funds said they had not been given the complete Rule 4(3) opinion behind SEBI's adjudication. After SEBI agreed to supply the full opinion and file notings, the Tribunal disposed of the appeals.
